body:
## Parent

Approved design: #38 and `docs/specs/centro-de-controle-da-vida-design.md`.

## What to build

Implement LunaÔÇÖs local daily workflow through the normal agent notification/question and chat surfaces: configurable morning planning, reminders for personal routines, and configurable end-of-day review. Do not add a dedicated Luna chat/panel or send personal routine definitions to the vault.

## Dependencies already completed

- #83 makes Luna a first-class agent in the regular sidebar/chat and renames Escrita to Agatha (closed).
- #47 established the canonical personal-routine source/state (closed): definitions stay in `rotinas-pessoais.md`; execution/status stays local.
- Telegram delivery and remote responses belong to #55, not this ticket.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately); all prerequisites for this local workflow are complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- The user can configure local morning-planning and end-of-day review times in an existing personal-routines/settings surface; no separate Luna-only interface is created.
- Morning planning presents the dayÔÇÖs agenda/classes, dated tasks and due personal routines, then asks the user to choose priorities. The former fixed 08:00 daily summary is part of this one interaction, not a duplicate message.
- A personal routine is due only according to its user-defined cadence/time. Missing or ambiguous schedule fields are not guessed; routines without an explicit time can appear in the planning/review but do not trigger a timed reminder.
- At a routineÔÇÖs scheduled time, Luna asks whether it was completed, deferred or not completed using the existing agent question/notification flow. Only an explicit response changes its local occurrence status; no task is created or completed implicitly.
- If unanswered, Luna retries once after 30 minutes. After that it stops reminding and leaves the occurrence pending for the dayÔÇÖs closing review. No-response is never interpreted as completion.
- End-of-day review summarizes completed and pending routines/tasks and asks about next steps. It does not modify tasks, agenda or vault records without an explicit user instruction and existing confirmation gates.
- Times use the OS local clock/time zone. Due events are idempotent across restart, clock changes, duplicate timer wakeups and local-day rollover.
- If the Office was closed, opening it produces one consolidated catch-up of still-relevant missed processes, not a burst of old notifications. There is no background service/relay.
- Tests use a fake clock and temporary stores to cover schedule boundaries, retry, no answer, explicit responses, duplicates, app closed/reopen, day rollover and time-zone changes.
- Never read/write the real vault in tests; preserve atomic persistence/backup conventions for local status.
